headline: Five-year Waste Management trash and recycling contract approved, 5-2, with year one at $2,689,790
summary: The contract covers curbside trash and recycling and dumpster pickup at certain locations, with annual rates rising from $2,689,790 in year one to $3,269,461 in year five. Waste Management of Londonderry, Inc. plans to take over service on July 1st, and the mayor said a separate recycling agreement for 55-plus condo communities would take effect July 1st, 2027. Before the vote, a motion to table the contract until December failed, 3-4.
decisions: Motion to table the Waste Management contract until December failed, 3-4.
Approved the Waste Management curbside trash and recycling contract, 5-2.
discussion: Condo recycling pickup: Public speakers from 55-plus communities asked the city to pick up their trash and recycling. The mayor said a separate, opt-in recycling agreement is planned, modeled on Haverhill's program, and would take effect July 1st, 2027.

Cost gap with Harvey: The CAFO estimated the five-year difference at about $5.5 million, with estimated tonnage and without yard waste. Members compared the bids and questioned the cost of the new contract.

Housing Authority trash costs: The Housing Authority director said added trash costs would reduce money for repairs for elderly and disabled residents. Public speakers asked the council to reconsider having the Housing Authority pay for its own trash collection.

Five-year term and exit: Members questioned why the contract has no convenience clause and a five-year term. The solicitor said the contract is subject to appropriation each year, so the city can still end it if funds are not appropriated.

decision_evidence.quote: So, I am going to request that this contract be tabled until December the first meeting in December ... Okay, so we have one, two, three yeses, one, two, three, four nos, and two absents, so it fails.
So, I'm going to call the question, Madame Vice, on this contract. ... 1 2 3 4 5 yeses, 2 nos, so it passes.
